clue.text: Vote was rigged, splitting hard cash for director on board

indicators.note: the vote and rigged letters break the cash word apart, sitting inside it

parts.note: coin is hard cash, money in metal rather than notes
X is the cross marked on a ballot paper

indicators.note: a rigged result has been fixed or tampered with, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone fiddled an election by slipping hard cash to a company director.
explanation.walkthrough: The director is on board a rowing boat, not a company board: the cox steers the crew. 'rigged' gives SWA from WAS.
explanation.definitionFit: The cox steers and calls the stroke for a rowing crew, directing them from aboard the boat.

clue.text: Flower got from bed

definitions.meaning: got up out of bed in the morning, past tense of arise

explanation.definitionFit: The garden bloom and the past tense of rising from bed share one spelling.

clue.text: Ogre concealed in plant

parts.note: an orc is a monstrous ogre-like creature of fantasy
hid means concealed, kept out of sight

explanation.surface: A monster lurks hidden among the garden plants.
explanation.definitionFit: An orchid is a flowering plant, often exotic, of a very large family.

clue.text: Artists turned up in record in form of dance music

indicators.note: the artists sit inside the record abbreviation

parts.note: CD, compact disc, a recorded album

indicators.note: in a down entry, turned up means the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: RAs are Royal Academicians, members of the Royal Academy of Arts
as means in the form of, in the role of

explanation.surface: Painters turning up on a recording of dance music.
explanation.walkthrough: RA, Royal Academician, is the usual crossword shorthand for an artist; 'turned up' suits a down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: The csardas is a Hungarian folk dance, and also the music played for it.

clue.text: Adventurously revised, eliminating parts of story considered worthless

indicators.note: the letters of the first word are reworked into a new order
the letters of the second word are taken out of the pool before rearranging

parts.note: taken as written as the letter pool
taken as written as the letters removed

explanation.surface: A tale boldly rewritten, with chunks cut, is judged to have no merit.
explanation.walkthrough: Removing S, T, O, R, Y from ADVENTUROUSLY leaves A, D, V, E, N, U, U, L, which 'revised' rearranges.
explanation.definitionFit: Something unvalued is not esteemed or prized, regarded as of no worth.

clue.text: Wonderful son, unusually pure — daughter likewise

indicators.note: pure arranged in an unusual way gives a new order of its letters

parts.note: says to repeat the previous step: the same rearrangement of pure again

explanation.surface: A proud parent finds a son unusually pure, and the daughter just as good.
explanation.walkthrough: 'likewise' gives no word of its own: it tells the solver to repeat the 'unusually' step, giving UPER a second time.
explanation.definitionFit: Super-duper is a jokey colloquial way of saying excellent or marvellous.

clue.text: Part of subscription mutually set up for season

indicators.note: in a down entry, set up means the letters are read from bottom to top
only a stretch of letters from these words is used

explanation.surface: Some of a mutual subscription is arranged for the coming season.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Part of' picks NMUTUA from subscriptiON MUTUAlly; 'set up' turns it round.
explanation.definitionFit: Autumn is the season between summer and winter, the fall.

clue.text: Some issue about judge and our temporary residences

indicators.note: the issue word goes around the judge and our letters

parts.note: issue means offspring, so some of it is sons
taken as written

explanation.surface: A family dispute concerning a judge and ourselves.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Some issue' reads as a dispute; issue means children here.
explanation.definitionFit: Sojourns are short stays somewhere, and so places one lives temporarily.

clue.text: Leaders coming from north, as usual, resting up in Pacific island

indicators.note: the leaders of the following words are their first letters

explanation.surface: Heading north as usual to relax on a Pacific island.
explanation.definitionFit: Nauru is a tiny island republic in the western Pacific Ocean, in Micronesia.

clue.text: Man is one that's insulted, being oddly selective

indicators.note: choosing only the odd-numbered letters of the word

explanation.surface: A man feels insulted at being picked on for no good reason.
explanation.walkthrough: Man is the Isle of Man, between Britain and Ireland, not a person.
explanation.definitionFit: The Isle of Man is an island in the Irish Sea, so Man is an example of one.

clue.text: Hard demand about barbecue, so arranged in part of garden (such as you'll find here)

indicators.note: the hard and demand letters wrap around the rearranged letters

parts.note: H is the abbreviation for hard, as on pencils
an order is a demand or command

indicators.note: the letters are put into a new order

parts.note: taken as written as anagram fodder
taken as written as anagram fodder

explanation.surface: Someone insists on a barbecue being set up in the garden.
explanation.walkthrough: The parenthesis points to the garden theme running through this puzzle; 'arranged' gives ERBACEOUSB.
explanation.definitionFit: A herbaceous border is a flower bed of perennial plants along the edge of a garden.

clue.text: Extended garden in new way

indicators.note: the word is set out with its letters in a new order

explanation.surface: A garden laid out afresh.
explanation.definitionFit: Ranged can mean extended or stretched over an area, as in hills ranged across the plain.

clue.text: See 25
Relatively slowly cut about half of bush that's profuse

indicators.note: the shortened tempo word goes around the piece of the shrub
cut means the last letter is chopped off

parts.note: andante is the musical direction for a moderately slow tempo

indicators.note: the first half of the word is taken

explanation.surface: Trimming a bush at a fairly slow pace when it has grown profusely.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Relatively slowly' looks like an adverb on cut, but it is the tempo marking andante, moderately slow in music.
explanation.definitionFit: Abundant means plentiful, present in great quantity, much as profuse does.

clue.text: Closely knit bunch batting, mature but losing wicket

parts.note: in cricket the side batting is said to be in

indicators.note: the wicket letter is dropped from the mature word

parts.note: to grow up is to mature
W is the cricket abbreviation for wicket

explanation.surface: A tight-knit cricket team at the crease ageing well but out once.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket, a team batting is 'in'; a batting side loses wickets as batters are dismissed.
explanation.definitionFit: An in-group is an exclusive clique whose members feel tightly bound together.

clue.text: At sea endures a submarine

indicators.note: at sea means confused, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A submarine crew endures life at sea.
explanation.walkthrough: 'submarine' is the adjective, beneath the sea, not the vessel.
explanation.definitionFit: Submarine as an adjective means lying or operating beneath the surface of the ocean.

clue.text: Fatty acid must be emptied out, I submit

indicators.note: with its contents removed only the first and last letters of the word stay

parts.note: to pose a question is to submit it for consideration

explanation.surface: A chemist insists the acid be drained, by way of a humble submission.
explanation.definitionFit: Adipose describes tissue made of or storing body fat.

clue.text: Envisaged sequence of events — oddly, no race is included

indicators.note: arranged in an odd way, so the letters are shuffled

explanation.surface: Strangely, no race features in the planned sequence of the day.
explanation.definitionFit: A scenario is an imagined or projected chain of happenings, a postulated outline.

clue.text: In legal document he had manifested embarrassment

parts.note: a writ is a formal written court order
the contraction he'd stands for he had

explanation.surface: A man showed shame at what was written in a court paper.
explanation.definitionFit: To have writhed is to have squirmed, as one does when acutely uncomfortable or ashamed.

clue.text: Climber found in only one part of garden

definitions.meaning: one who goes upwards, such as a mountaineer

definitions.text: found in only one part of garden
definitions.meaning: in typography, the stroke rising above the line, which among the letters of the word garden appears only on the d

explanation.walkthrough: The 'part of garden' is a letter of the word itself: g has a descender, and only d rises above the line.
explanation.definitionFit: In type an ascender is the upward stroke of letters like d, and one who ascends climbs.

clue.text: All one can consume, no end of drink? That's bad

indicators.note: no means the following letter is taken away

parts.note: a skinful is as much alcohol as one can hold

indicators.note: the end of the word is its last letter

explanation.surface: A drinker downs a skinful and finds that wicked.
explanation.walkthrough: SKINFUL is British slang for a large amount of alcohol drunk at once.
explanation.definitionFit: Sinful means wicked or morally wrong, a strong sense of bad.

clue.text: See 11
Villain that might create problem in camp

definitions.meaning: the baddie of a film or story

definitions.text: that might create problem in camp
definitions.meaning: a faulty or failing rope holding a tent down would cause trouble on a campsite

explanation.walkthrough: A guy is a guy rope steadying a tent, so a bad one is trouble at camp.
explanation.definitionFit: The villain of a story is commonly called the baddie or the bad guy.

clue.text: Is intrepid, wildly encouraged

indicators.note: the letters are thrown about wildly into a new order

explanation.surface: A bold person is fired up and urged on.
explanation.definitionFit: To inspirit is to fill with courage or animation, to hearten someone.

clue.text: Game that gets exciting at match point

definitions.text: Game that gets exciting at match point

parts.words: Game that gets exciting at match point
parts.note: suggests tennis, but this card game peaks when two turned cards match and players shout

explanation.definitionFit: In this children's card game players race to call out when two cards of equal value appear.

clue.text: Part of play got by audience and understood

indicators.note: what the audience gets is what they hear, so the word is taken by its sound

parts.note: a scene is a division of an act in a play

explanation.surface: A section of the drama is grasped by the theatregoers.
explanation.definitionFit: Seen can mean grasped or taken in, as in I see what you mean.

clue.text: Where one's led astray, not in bed

definitions.text: Where one's led astray, not in bed

parts.words: Where one's led astray, not in bed
parts.note: to be deceived is to be led along a garden walkway, which in a garden is not in a flower bed

explanation.definitionFit: Leading someone up the garden path means deceiving them, and the path runs between the beds.

clue.text: Spirit, French counterpart of whisky

definitions.meaning: whisky comes from Gaelic for water of life, and the French phrase means the same

explanation.walkthrough: Whisky derives from the Gaelic uisge beatha, water of life, which in French is the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Eau de vie is French brandy distilled from fruit, a strong spirit named as water of life.
